es: Resolver una ronda de preguntas sorpresa con respuestas estructuradas, una reparación y una reformulación, manteniendo la compostura bajo presión y recapitulando al final.

teaching.en: Welcome to a rapid-fire round: every contestant faces three questions, and each answer must fit into sixty seconds.
teaching.es: Bienvenidos a una ronda relámpago: cada concursante se enfrenta a tres preguntas y cada respuesta debe caber en sesenta segundos.
teaching.explanationEs: La ronda combina todo el bloque: ganar tiempo, estructura, reparación y cierre.

teaching.en: Keep your composure under pressure: buy a second, commit to a stance and give one reason before anything else.
teaching.es: Mantén la compostura bajo presión: gana un segundo, comprométete con una postura y da una razón antes que nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Con presión, sigue el orden que ya conoces.

teaching.en: If you hesitate, fall back on your structure: point, reason, example and close will carry you through the gap.
teaching.es: Si dudas, recurre a tu estructura: punto, razón, ejemplo y cierre te sacarán del apuro.
teaching.explanationEs: Fall back on = recurrir a algo seguro cuando falla la improvisación.

teaching.en: Rephrase instead of stopping: a new wording keeps the round moving and shows that you are still in control.

teaching.explanationEs: Instead of + -ing: reformular mantiene la conversación viva.

teaching.en: If an answer drifts, admit it and recap in one sentence; that is how you get back on track.
teaching.es: Si una respuesta se desvía, admítelo y recapitula en una frase; así es como retomas el rumbo.
teaching.explanationEs: Recap resume lo dicho; get back on track devuelve la respuesta a su hilo.

teaching.en: A good habit, like structuring every answer, helps you hold your nerve when the next question arrives without warning.

teaching.explanationEs: El hábito de estructurar sostiene las respuestas improvisadas.

prompt.es: Escucha la respuesta y elige qué corrige el hablante.

choices.text: His own stance on paper and screens.
The time of day in his example.
The number of books he finished reading.

feedback.es: Tras «Sorry, I meant two evenings» cambia el momento del día de su ejemplo; la postura y la duración siguen igual.

origin.audio: Is it better to read on paper or on a screen? That's a tricky one, but my stance is paper. The main reason is focus. For example, last month I finished a whole novel in two afternoons on the train. Sorry, I meant two evenings. In short, paper keeps my attention where it belongs.

feedback.es: Composure es la calma al hablar bajo presión e instead of + -ing expresa hacer una cosa en lugar de otra.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cierra con una síntesis tras la respuesta?

choices.text: By the way, I also like pasta, although I rarely cook it at home.
Anyway, I forgot what I wanted to say, so never mind.
To recap, cooking saves money and builds a habit that lasts for life.

feedback.es: To recap resume la idea en una frase; las otras abren un desvío o muestran desorden.

origin.text: The contestant has answered the question about cooking with a stance, a reason and an example. The host now gives her five seconds to finish before the next round begins.

prompt.es: Responde a tres preguntas sorpresa: estructura, una reparación y una reformulación.

answer.text: Thanks, that's a tricky first question, so let me think. My stance is that students should wear a uniform. The main reason is that it saves time and money. For example, I spend ten minutes every morning deciding what to wear at weekends, but only two on school days. Sorry, I meant five on school days. In short, a uniform is a useful habit. Second question. Hang on, let me gather my thoughts. I would say that studying in a group is better than studying alone, because ideas travel faster. For example, last month my group solved a hard problem in an hour that I had failed to solve alone in an evening. Let me rephrase that: a group gives you a second mind. Third question, what would I change in my school? Off the top of my head, I would open the library on Saturdays. The reason is that many students have no quiet place at home. To recap, uniforms save time, groups save effort and an open library saves weekends. My point is that small changes matter.
accepted: Thanks, that's a tricky first question, so let me think. My stance is that students should wear a uniform. The main reason is that it saves time and money. For example, I spend ten minutes every morning deciding what to wear at weekends, but only two on school days. Sorry, I meant five on school days. In short, a uniform is a useful habit. Second question. Hang on, let me gather my thoughts. I would say that studying in a group is better than studying alone, because ideas travel faster. For example, last month my group solved a hard problem in an hour that I had failed to solve alone in an evening. Let me rephrase that: a group gives you a second mind. Third question, what would I change in my school? Off the top of my head, I would open the library on Saturdays. The reason is that many students have no quiet place at home. To recap, uniforms save time, groups save effort and an open library saves weekends. My point is that small changes matter.

Let me think for a moment. My view is that students should not wear uniforms. The first reason is that clothes are a way of expressing yourself. For example, my cousin designed her own jacket last year, and she has worn it proudly ever since. Sorry, I meant two years ago. So, in conclusion, freedom in clothes helps students feel confident. For the second question, I believe studying alone is better. Because it is quiet, you can focus for longer. Let me put that another way: silence removes distractions. For the third question, I would change the school canteen. The main reason is that the queues are too long. For instance, last week I waited twenty minutes for lunch. To sum up, freedom in clothes, quiet for studying and a faster canteen would improve daily life at school.

feedback.es: Una buena ronda responde con estructura, repara un error, reformula una idea y termina recapitulando.

origin.text: Preguntas: 1) ¿Deberían los estudiantes llevar uniforme? 2) ¿Es mejor estudiar solo o en grupo? 3) ¿Qué cambiarías de tu colegio? Escribe 240–300 palabras: responde a las tres con postura, razón y ejemplo, incluye una reparación (Sorry, I meant…) y una reformulación (Let me rephrase that) y cierra recapitulando.

prompt.es: Escucha la crónica y elige qué da a entender la reacción del público.

choices.text: That recovering calmly counted for more than a perfect start.
That a joke to buy time impressed the audience more than a recap.
That the first contestant was unfairly punished for her hesitation.
That the host had favoured the third contestant from the start.

feedback.es: La concursante que tropezó, reformuló y cerró con un recap obtuvo el aplauso más fuerte: el público valoró más la recuperación elegante que un inicio perfecto.

origin.audio: In the final of the radio quiz, the host threw a surprise round at the three contestants. The first, rattled by the opening question, hesitated for so long that her time ran out. The second kept his composure, bought a few seconds with a joke and gave a structured answer, but he mixed up two dates and had to repair them twice. The third gave a slower, plainer answer; when she stumbled, she rephrased instead of stopping, and closed with a one-sentence recap. The audience cheered her the loudest, and the host admitted that she had won the round before the scores were read out.

prompt.es: ¿Qué propone la productora en esta nota?

choices.text: Asking the contestants to give shorter answers so the show finishes on time.
Slowing the pace slightly so contestants can rely on their structure.
Replacing the rapid-fire round with a longer and calmer format.
Warning the contestants that their structure is too predictable.

feedback.es: Pide una pausa de dos segundos para que los concursantes puedan recurrir a su estructura; quiere ver cómo piensan, no lo rápido que hablan.

origin.text: Note to the presenter: in tonight's rapid-fire round, please do not rush the contestants. Several of them began well but lost their way when the next question came too quickly. A two-second pause costs us nothing on air, and it lets them fall back on their structure. Remember that we want to see how they think, not how fast they can talk.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si pierdes el hilo, recapitula en una frase y retoma el rumbo.»

feedback.es: Get back on track significa retomar el rumbo después de un desvío.

origin.text: If you lose the thread halfway through an answer, recap in one sentence and get back on ___ without apologising.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud revela la concursante ante los errores?

choices.text: She believes the audience accepted her slip only because she looked nervous.
She thinks a repair is worthwhile only when the error is a serious one.
She learned that a quickly repaired slip hardly disturbs the listeners.
She feels the fear vanished because she stopped caring about the result.

feedback.es: Dice que el miedo desapareció al corregirse porque nadie levantó la vista: concluye que un desliz reparado enseguida apenas molesta al oyente.

origin.text: After the show, the contestant told the interviewer: “Honestly, I was terrified. But I told myself that I only had to do four things: buy a second, pick a side, give a reason and close. The moment I said sorry, I meant, the fear vanished: nobody in the studio even looked up, and I realised that I could carry on.”
